name: Lakulīśa

tradition.text: the 28th and last of Śiva's yoga-teacher incarnations of the Vaivasvata manvantara, in the age when Kṛṣṇa Vāsudeva and Vyāsa Dvaipāyana are born (Liṅga P. 1.24.125-131; Kūrma P. 1.51.9-10)

scholarly.text: c. 2nd c. CE (reckoned back ten teacher-generations from the Mathurā pillar inscription of 380 CE); some scholars say 1st–2nd c.

places: Kāyāvarohaṇa / Kāyāvataraṇa / Kāyārohaṇa (Karvan, near Vadodara, Gujarat)

realization_account.text: Not a human who became realized but the Lord himself: seeing an abandoned corpse in a cremation ground, Śiva entered it by yogic power and became the brahmacārin Lakulī at the siddha-field called Kāyāvatāra (Liṅga P. 1.24.127-130); Kauṇḍinya says the Lord, in human form, took a brahmin's body, descended at Kāyāvataraṇa and walked to Ujjayinī, where he taught Kuśika; the Kāravaṇa-māhātmya says Śiva was born to Viśvarūpa and Sudarśanā, and after the infant died Śiva entered the body and later merged into the Brahmeśvara liṅga at Kāyāvarohaṇa.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: Lakulīśa, 'Lord with the club', is regarded as the incarnation of Śiva who founded the Pāśupata observance and taught the Pāśupata Sūtra, and the first of the Pāśupata tīrthakaras. His images show him seated, holding a club and a citron, often ithyphallic; the Liṅga Purāṇa (1.76.38-39) prescribes his image surrounded by disciples, hand raised in exposition. Kauṇḍinya does not use the name Lakulīśa; he speaks of 'the Lord' who descended at Kāyāvataraṇa.

name: Kuśika

tradition.text: first disciple of the incarnate Lord

scholarly.text: c. 2nd c. CE (ten generations before Uditācārya, 380 CE)

summary: The first of Lakulīśa's four disciples (Liṅga P. 1.24.131; Kūrma P. 1.51.26). Kauṇḍinya tells that Kuśika, prompted by Rudra, approached the Lord at Ujjayinī, declared his birth, lineage, learning and freedom from debts, and asked whether there is a final and absolute removal of all suffering - the question the Pāśupata Sūtra answers. The Mathurā inscription of 380 CE counts its donor as tenth in succession from Kuśika.

name: Garga (Pāśupata)
summary: The second of Lakulīśa's four disciples in the Purāṇic lists (Liṅga P. 1.24.131; Kūrma P. 1.51.26) and third in the Jain lists of eighteen tīrthakaras (as Gārgya); a Pāśupata line was traced to him.

name: Mitra (Pāśupata)
summary: The third of Lakulīśa's four disciples (Liṅga P. 1.24.131 'Mitra'; Kūrma P. 1.51.26 'Mitraka'; Jain lists 'Maitrya').

name: Kauruṣya
summary: The fourth of Lakulīśa's four disciples (Liṅga P. 1.24.131; Jain lists 'Kauruṣa').

name: Kauṇḍinya
summary: Author of the Pañcārthabhāṣya, the only surviving commentary on the Pāśupata Sūtra, which frames the teaching as five categories and five stages. Sometimes identified with the tīrthakara Rāśīkara (uncertain).

name: Rāśīkara
summary: The seventeenth of the eighteen Pāśupata tīrthakaras in the Jain lists (Guṇaratna; Rājaśekhara); the Ratnaṭīkā has the ascetic salute 'the tīrthakaras from Lakulīśa to Rāśīkara', and the Sarvadarśanasaṃgraha cites a 'Rāśīkara-bhāṣya'. His identification with Kauṇḍinya is a scholarly suggestion.

name: Bhāsarvajña
summary: Naiyāyika author of the Nyāyasāra (with its self-commentary Nyāyabhūṣaṇa) and a Pāśupata: the Ratnaṭīkā on the Gaṇakārikā is ascribed to him, and Dalal's edition ascribes the Gaṇakārikā verses to him too.

name: Haradatta (Pāśupata ācārya)
summary: Pāśupata teacher whom the Sarvadarśanasaṃgraha (ch. 6) quotes as the author of the Gaṇakārikā verses on the gains and impurities. Not to be confused with other Haradattas (the Dharmasūtra commentator; Haradatta Śivācārya).

name: Uddyotakara
summary: Author of the Nyāyavārttika; the colophon of that work calls him 'Pāśupatācārya', a sign of the link between Nyāya and the Pāśupatas (this unit's contribution; the full entry belongs to the Nyāya unit).

name: Uditācārya
summary: Pāśupata teacher of the Mathurā pillar inscription of 380 CE, described as tenth in succession from Kuśika; he installed two liṅgas named after his teachers (Kapileśvara and Upamiteśvara) in a teachers' shrine.

name: Bhāva Bṛhaspati
summary: Pāśupata ācārya who, according to the Prabhāsa (Bhadrakālī) inscription of 1169 CE, became head of Somanātha and directed its restoration under the Caulukya king Kumārapāla.

name: Tripurāntaka (Pāśupata)
summary: Pāśupata ascetic eulogised in the Cintra praśasti of 1287 CE for his foundations at Somanātha; the inscription traces his line to one of Lakulīśa's disciples (details to be checked).

name: Īśāna (Pāśupata tīrthakara)
summary: Number 6 of the eighteen avatāras / tīrthakaras of Śiva worshipped by the Śaiva (Pāśupata-Naiyāyika) ascetics according to the Jain doxographers Guṇaratna (Tarkarahasyadīpikā) and Rājaśekhara (Ṣaḍdarśanasamuccaya, 1348). Nothing else is recorded.
notes: Known only from the Jain lists; not to be conflated with the Vedic/Purāṇic sage of the same name.

name: Kedāraśakti
summary: A Kālāmukha pontiff of the Kōḍiya-maṭha at Balligāve (Śakti-pariṣad) named in inscriptions (details to be checked).

name: Vāmaśakti

scholarly.text: 12th c. (inscriptions name more than one Vāmaśakti)

summary: Kālāmukha pontiff of the Kōḍiya-maṭha at Balligāve, praised in 12th-c. inscriptions for learning and influence (details to be checked).

name: Kriyāśakti
summary: Kālāmukha teacher remembered as preceptor (rājaguru) at the early Vijayanagara court and of the minister Mādhava; among the last prominent Kālāmukhas (identification of his order moderate-low).
